headline: U.S.-mediated Lebanon-Israel 14-point framework agreement: 1. End the conflict and formally transition toward a cessation of hostilities. 2. Israel will withdraw from Lebanon in phases, contingent on evolving security conditions. 3. The Lebanese Armed Forces will progressively assume full responsibility for national security. 4. Hezbollah and all other non-state armed groups must be fully and verifiably disarmed. 5. Israel affirms it has no territorial ambitions in Lebanon and will withdraw once security threats are resolved. 6. Lebanon reaffirms the state’s exclusive authority to maintain armed forces and declare war. 7. A US-backed coordination and verification mechanism will oversee implementation. 8. Both parties commit to a sovereign, stable Lebanon free from armed groups threatening either side. 9. The US will support and strengthen the Lebanese Armed Forces, with assistance tied to verified progress. 10. The US will lead coordination of international reconstruction, humanitarian aid, and economic recovery efforts. 11. Lebanon and the US will ensure that aid and reconstruction funds do not reach Hezbollah or other armed groups. 12. Israel and Lebanon will establish working groups to negotiate a comprehensive peace and security framework. 13. Both sides will cease hostile political and legal actions and cooperate on the return of detainees and remains. 14. Israel and Lebanon acknowledge the US role and express appreciation for President Donald Trump’s leadership.

headline: A Russian FPV drone operator struck a light anti-drone air defense system, identified as MAAWLR, operated by the Armed Forces of Ukraine and produced by the American company Sierra Nevada Corp. The MAAWLR system is mounted on a pickup truck chassis and is equipped with an electro-optical targeting system for autonomous target detection, while also being capable of receiving external target designation from radar assets. It can use a range of missiles, including AIM-9M, AIM-132 ASRAAM, AIM-120 AMRAAM, IRIS-T, R-27, and APKWS II. Depending on the munition used, the system is assessed to be capable of engaging drones at ranges of approximately 6–15 km.
